data.title: California AG subpoenas Nvidia over concerns about former CEO, China ties
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday his office had served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia ( NVDA ) related to reports of former CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

"The conduct of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and its former CEO raises bright red flags," Bonta said, adding that his office was examining whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) or Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information, and if the company misled investors and the public about the risk.

The probe will help determine whether Nvidia's ( NVDA ) actions violated California law, the attorney general's office said.

Huang resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang's ties to China's Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to Reuters.

China has rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting Jensen Huang.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has ruled out bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, despite a campaign by employees and prominent technology figures, including Elon Musk, to reinstate him.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission is also reportedly probing Nvidia ( NVDA ) after Huang's resignation.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday that the Trump administration had approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD AI chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May this year, although it was unclear how many were ultimately shipped.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) said the approvals were subject to strict conditions and limited volumes and that it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

(Reporting by Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

data.description:

    (Updates for afternoon trade)
    By Rajasik Mukherjee
       Nov 20 (Reuters) - Taiwan stocks tumbled more than 6% on
Friday and clocked their worst week in more than three decades
as investors unwound AI-related bets over concerns around
valuations, profitability and rising debt.
    Taiwan's benchmark equity index ended 6.2% down to
hit its lowest close since mid-April, deepening its weekly loss
to 17.5%, the steepest five-day rout since 1990.
    The index has lost $1.12 trillion in value since October 6,
when it touched an all-time high, according to LSEG-compiled
data. Over that period, it has lost nearly 28% as of Friday's
close.
    Stocks in South Korea fell more than 5% to their
lowest point in more than nine months, with Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF )
 and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) shedding 7% each.
    That pushed the MSCI EM Asia equity index
down more than 4% to levels last seen in early April. The gauge
has lost nearly 9% this week, putting it on course for its worst
week since mid-March 2020.
    The weakness spread to Southeast Asian equity markets:
stocks in Thailand and Singapore fell around 2%
each, while those in the Philippines dived more than 3%
to their weakest level since April 2020.
    Regional currencies also came under pressure due to foreign
selling: the Indonesian rupiah hovered near a record low
of 18,285 per US dollar, while the Philippine peso and
the Korean won edged lower.
    "There's a knock-on effect in Asia," said Dilin Wu, research
strategist at Pepperstone.
    "When foreign investors sell local shares and move their
money back into dollars, that puts additional pressure on
regional currencies."


    WHEN THE CHIPS ARE DOWN
    The AI trade has been hit by concerns over valuations,
rising debt, growing opposition to data centres and the fallout
from Jensen Huang's departure from chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ),
sparking an aggressive unwinding of crowded positions.
    Even Anthropic's record-breaking IPO, followed by a debut
that fizzled later in the session on Thursday, did not spark a
broader rally.
    That caution reverberated in Asia, as investors sold
chipmakers in Taiwan and South Korea, key beneficiaries of the
global AI trade.
    TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker and a
key Nvidia ( NVDA ) supplier, hit a more than seven-month low by dropping
as much as 6.2%, and logged its worst week since October 1997.
Shares of chip designer MediaTek dropped 10%.
     "The selloff is partly about AI valuations, but the scale
of the decline tells us there's more going on," Wu added.
     "Even Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blockbuster earnings haven't been enough to
reassure investors about the sustainability of AI spending ...
add foreign selling and margin calls to the mix, and the decline

data.title: Japan's Nikkei ends 5% lower as Anthropic's IPO fails to restore AI confidence
data.description:
(Updates with closing prices)

By Junko Fujita

TOKYO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Japan's Nikkei stock average fell 5% to close at a seven-month low on Friday, as technology shares tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in the AI trade.

The Nikkei ended 5.06% lower at 56,436.65, its lowest close since April 13. For the week, the index lost 7.7%.

The broader Topix fell 3.88% to 3,674.22.

"There was a high expectation that Anthropic's market debut may lift sentiment for AI-related shares, but that hope faded as its price pared gains," said Hiroyuki Ueno, chief strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

Shares of Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, opened 34% higher than the $83 IPO price set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

In Japan, chip-related Advantest ( ADTTF ) and Tokyo Electron ( TOELF ) slid 10.32% and 7.06%, respectively. Technology investor SoftBank Group tumbled 14.48% and memory chip maker Kioxia ( KXHCF ) lost 11.66%.

"Investors realise that these chip shares became cheap, but they are afraid to pick them up because they are afraid there may be another dip in the market," said Ueno.

Of 225 stocks on the Nikkei, 214 fell and 11 rose.

Among the advancers were insurer Tokio Marine Holdings ( TKOMF ) , which rose 2.03%. Peers MS&AD Insurance and Sompo Holdings ( NHOLF ) rose 0.4% and 2.01%, respectively.

Railway operators rose, with Keisei Electric Railway ( KELRF ) and Odakyu Electric Railway ( ODERF ) edging up 0.26% and 0.08%, respectively.

Takeda Pharmaceutical ( TAK ) rose 0.33%.

Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 93% fell, 5% rose and 1% traded flat.

(Reporting by Junko Fujita; Editing by Rashmi Aich and Ronojoy Mazumdar)

data.title: Anthropic shares may fall 5% at Friday’s open, crypto futures suggest
data.description:
Anthropic’s first day as a public company ended at $97.17 on Nasdaq, and crypto traders are marking the AI company’s shares about 5% lower, in the low $90s, as of Friday morning in Asia.

The contract is ANT, a perpetual futures market run by trade.xyz on Hyperliquid, a crypto derivatives exchange. It tracks the price of one Anthropic share and has no expiry date. Traders post crypto as collateral and own no actual stock, and the contract keeps trading when U.S. exchanges go dark.

Trade.xyz caps total open interest at $400 million, and the cap is already about two-thirds full.

It started life as a pre-IPO bet, which CoinDesk covered in October, and has turned into an overnight market for the stock after Anthropic’s offering.

The market got busy. About $1.7 billion traded through it over the past 24 hours, and open interest, the value of positions still open, jumped by more than half to about $259 million as of Friday’s Asian morning, data shows.

Funding is a small periodic payment that keeps the contract’s price tied to the stock. It stayed positive at about 5.5% a year, so longs kept paying shorts to hold their positions even with the contract trading below Thursday’s Nasdaq close.

Hyperliquid’s round-the-clock markets are proving to be a reliable indicator of where prices may be headed once the New York session begins, with traders having priced Thursday’s open almost perfectly.

Anthropic was priced at $83 on Wednesday in an IPO that raised about $81 billion, the largest on record, ahead of SpaceX’s $75 billion in June.

A minute before the stock’s first Nasdaq trade, the ANT contract sat at about $111 on both trade.xyz and OKX, per data reviewed by CoinDesk. The stock opened at $111.50 and peaked at $ 114.99 before reversing to close 17% above its IPO price.

The largest position on the market now is a $30 million short opened at $102.36 with 6x leverage, trackers show. The wallet associated with that trader sold into the afternoon fade and is sitting at a 10% gain as of Asian afternoon hours.

data.title: Anthropic's blockbuster debut tests Wall Street's faith in AI boom
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a turbulent stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

The early exuberance faded, however, signaling volatility ahead as investors locked in quick gains and the main indexes retreated amid renewed jitters over the sector's outlook.

Shares of the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company opened at $111.50, which was 34% higher than the IPO price of $83 set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and ended the day at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

Anthropic's fully diluted $2 trillion valuation includes stock options and restricted stock units that the company has promised employees but which have not been vested into actual shares. Based on Anthropic's outstanding shares, the company's value reached as much as $1.5 trillion on Thursday, on par with Tesla.

The AI market euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks, with last week's resignation of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang causing concern. The technology has boosted economic growth but has prompted unease about mounting debt loads and doomsday warnings. An anti-data-center movement may have helped Democrats sweep the US midterm elections.

"The blockbuster Anthropic launch is a critical step in reassuring the market about the potential for AI, but it's really just the beginning," said Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research. "We still need to see what happens with OpenAI, how the Nvidia ( NVDA ) situation evolves, how the political climate for data centers shapes up, and what the historical performance for Anthropic proves to be before we'll get any real sense of stability."

The six-year-old company has positioned itself as the gatekeeper of AI safety while selling investors the idea that it can be profitable despite massive compute costs. Led by Dario Amodei, a former OpenAI employee, Anthropic has also signaled it may tap debt markets.

"At some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade, and debt is an instrument that we have available to us, and we'd like to use at some point in the future," CEO Amodei told CNBC in an interview on Thursday.

Anthropic's net loss narrowed in the third quarter as revenue jumped 47% from the previous quarter, even as the pace of growth slowed sharply from the prior quarter. The company has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google.

INDUSTRY BENCHMARK, EMPLOYEE PAYDAY

As the first frontier AI company to go public, Anthropic is poised to become the sector's benchmark. The company sold 980 million shares at $83 each, pricing the IPO above its initial range of $70 to $78 set when it launched the road show.

Its IPO proceeds could climb to as much as $93.5 billion if underwriters fully exercise their option to purchase additional shares. Currently, the figure sits at over $107 billion, including the additional $26 billion raised through a private placement. AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and TSMC were the investors in the private placement.

"Some of the demand may simply reflect investors not wanting to miss out on the rare opportunity to gain exposure to a leading AI company, even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," IPOX associate Lukas Muehlbauer said.

London-based index rebalance analytics firm Intropic estimates passive demand from index-tracking funds will account for the purchase of up to 30% of Anthropic's shares offered by the end of the year.

Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff.

Based on the IPO price, Amodei and his six co-founders, who together own about 10% of the company, had stakes worth nearly $150 billion combined, according to a Reuters calculation based on details in the filing.

JUSTIFYING THE PRICE TAG

Debate has intensified over whether the AI boom is becoming a bubble as soaring valuations and a web of circular deals involving AI developers, chipmakers, cloud providers and investors fuel questions about the durability of the industry's growth.

Anthropic's breakneck growth has so far insulated it from these concerns, but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

Anthropic "isn't a prudent 'buy-at-any-price' opportunity for retail wealth clients," said Talley Leger, chief market strategist at The Wealth Consulting Group. "History shows that retail investors buying hot tech IPOs on day one historically underperform broad market indexes over a 3-year horizon."

The company will also need to balance growth with calls to slow the development of advanced AI models. Anthropic warned in its IPO prospectus that AI could behave unpredictably and advance faster than oversight mechanisms.

The massive IPO will earn the underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, a $550 million fee, a regulatory filing showed.

(Reporting by Niket Nishant, Manya Saini in Bengaluru and Echo Wang in New York; Additional reporting by Chibuike Oguh, Noel Randewich, Anhata Rooprai and Pritam Biswas; Editing by Christian Plumb, Arun Koyyur, Sayantani Ghosh and Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Fed's Paulson says understanding, not guidance, drives effective communication
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday central bank communications work better when officials and the public understand one another, rather than when Fed officials provide explicit comments about what they think lies ahead.

For the Fed, "understanding matters more than the specific ways we communicate," Paulson said in the text of a speech to be delivered before a gathering held by the Money Marketeers of New York University.

"When we understand each other, we don't need to say as much when new data arrive," she said, adding, "You can anticipate how we'll respond, and we can act in ways that are steady and, for the most part, predictable."

WARSH'S COMMUNICATION OVERHAUL

Paulson's views on Fed communications come as the central bank has been overhauling how it explains its actions to the public. Under new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, the Fed has shortened its Federal Open Market Committee policy statement and has launched a special task force to weigh how the Fed should communicate its actions and views.

At the same time, Warsh has, in contrast to other recent Fed leaders, stepped almost entirely away from providing any guidance about the interest-rate outlook.

But even as Warsh has pulled back, many of his colleagues on the central bank have continued to provide regular updates on where they think interest-rate policy is heading and how the economy is faring.

Paulson did not offer any comments about the near-term outlook for interest-rate policy, as the central bank approaches its December 8-9 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, where it is widely expected to hike rates by a quarter percentage point, to between 4% and 4.25%.

Paulson said in her remarks that understanding how the Fed reacts to incoming data is particularly important.

"Communication works best when it builds a shared understanding of the reaction function, and that credibility is essential, because people act on messages they trust," she said.

Paulson said an understanding of what the Fed is doing and why helped markets navigate the Fed's decision to hold rates steady in late October after boosting them in September and signaling more hikes were in the works.

"In October, markets expected further tightening, so the pause did not leave policy behind where it needed to be," she said. "A shared understanding of the reaction function allowed policy to move deliberately and gave people time to adjust, without the risk that a pause was mistaken for a stop."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby in New York; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: FOREX-Dollar near 19-month high, set for 4th weekly gain as AI jitters spur haven bid
data.description:
* Dollar index near strongest since early April 2025

* Markets debating size, not likelihood, of December Fed hike

* Yen firms after Japan core inflation hits 2.2%

(Updates to Asia afternoon)

By Li Gu and Rae Wee

SHANGHAI/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The dollar edged lower but hovered near a 19-month high on Friday, on track for a fourth straight week of gains as expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening underpinned the greenback and jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, its strongest since early April 2025. The weeks-long rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike in December should be considered.

The strong dollar also comes amid weak equity sentiment, with AI spending concerns dragging the S&P 500 lower for six straight sessions. The index is down about 5% so far this week, and Anthropic's record market debut on Thursday did little to revive investor confidence.

Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a volatile stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

"Risk aversion intensified, supporting the safe-haven dollar and driving demand for US Treasuries," OCBC analysts said in a note. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks."

The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to a one-week low of 5.02% and is down 13 basis points on the week.

Adding to the dollar's strength were hawkish signals from the Fed. Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own.

"The debate now is not really about whether the Federal Reserve will raise rates in December, but how much it will raise rates by," said Carol Kong, currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

"We still think 25 basis points is more likely," Kong said. "If they really want to quicken the pace of tightening, I think they will prefer to increase rates by 25 bps in consecutive meetings rather than deliver a bigger-than-usual hike."

YEN FIRMS ON INFLATION DATA

The yen firmed 0.3% against the dollar to 159.13, set to close the week with a small gain after three weeks of losses that had dragged the currency near the key 160 level.

Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that strengthen the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Analysts at Capital Economics argue the yen's recent weakness is unlikely to last. With long-term inflation expectations now around target, further increases in yields would be mostly in real terms, which, combined with their view that US yields will fall, should prove yen-positive, the analysts said.

The Bank of Japan will likely raise interest rates for the third time this year at its December meeting and follow up with another by end-March, according to a ​majority of economists in a Reuters poll.

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3106, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0977. The Aussie hovered close to a one-year low of $0.6664.

China's offshore yuan firmed 0.3% to 6.6743 per dollar, bouncing from a more than one-month low against the US dollar that it hit a day earlier as corporate repatriation offset the impact of a continuing dollar rally. China left key benchmark lending rates unchanged in November for an 18th consecutive month.

(Reporting by Li Gu in Shanghai and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Tom Hogue)

data.title: Morning Bid: Anthropic's splashy IPO fails to lift AI boat
data.description:
A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Jiaxing Li

Are we nearing the end of the AI boom?

Apparently, even Anthropic's debut as the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company couldn't do much, at least for now, to flip the increasingly worrisome narrative on AI trades.

Its turbulent first day of trading may bode more volatility ahead, with investors beginning to question whether the boom has peaked as the list of positive catalysts thins and exits from crowded trades gather momentum.

MORE POLICY SCRUTINY AHEAD?

This week's blowout earnings from industry bellwether Nvidia were meant to showcase the sector's strong momentum and reignite optimism around the AI trade, but have instead been overshadowed by uncertainty following CEO Jensen Huang's exit.

And as if that chaos was not enough, its powerful rival AMD is now probably next in line for greater US regulatory scrutiny after a short report raised concern about the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some of which have links to firms on US blacklists.

Asian stocks are now feeling the force of the rout, with MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan on track for its worst week since the height of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

That pain now looks set to extend beyond Asia as the day unfolds. In early European trade, pan-region Euro Stoxx 50 futures were down 1.6%. US stock futures also point to further loss, with the S&P 500 e-minis down 0.6%.

DOLLAR, TREASURY CATCH HAVEN FLOW

data.title: Australia's NextDC shareholders deliver second pay strike but stop short of board spill
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Shareholders of Australian data centre developer NextDC ( NXDCF ) rejected its executive pay plan for a second straight year but voted against removing the board, a stock exchange filing showed on Friday.

Investors holding 72.06% of shares voted against the remuneration report, broadly matching last year's near 72% opposition, amid calls for greater accountability and closer alignment between executive pay and shareholder returns.

Under Australia's "two strikes" rule, opposition of at least 25% to a pay report in two consecutive years triggers a vote on whether to remove the board and force directors to stand for re-election.

However, 96.21% of votes cast opposed the board spill, allowing directors to remain in place while keeping pressure on them to address investor concerns over executive pay.

The votes come nearly a month after CEO Craig Scroggie said he would forgo his fiscal 2027 bonus and the company withdrew a plan to increase the non-executive directors' maximum aggregate annual remuneration.

"The M3 issues have hit confidence, and when a big project stumbles, shareholders want to see pay take the hit across the board, not just one line item," Mark Gardener, CEO of MPC Markets, said.

NextDC ( NXDCF ) lifted its annual net revenue and underlying operating earnings outlook on Friday, driven by strong sales and revenue growth outside the affected M3 contracts, alongside cost-saving measures.

That followed last month's cut to its earnings forecast and capital expenditure plans, and a pause on all projects lacking customer contracts after a major setback at its flagship M3 data centre in Melbourne.

NextDC ( NXDCF ) shares ended 7.1% lower at A$9.01, marking its weakest session since October 23, and tracked the broader technology sub-index, which ended 4.7% lower.

The market cares more about the earnings path than the pay fight, and the guidance upgrade on growth outside M3, along with cost savings, tells investors the core business is working, Gardener said.

($1 = 1.5011 Australian dollars)

data.title: Xi hails 'comprehensive turnaround' in China-Australia ties
data.description:
SHENZHEN/SYDNEY, Nov 20 (Reuters) - China's relationship with Australia has seen a "comprehensive turnaround" over the last four years, President Xi Jinping said on Friday, after meeting Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

Xi said China was willing to work with Australia to expand cooperation, set aside differences and build on recent improvements in relations, taking the partnership to a new stage of development.

"Since you took office as prime minister in 2022, we have met four times. I think it is fair to say that together we have brought about a comprehensive turnaround in China-Australia relations," Xi said.

Ties with China, Australia's top trade partner, soured under the country's previous centre-right coalition government, which called for an inquiry into the origins of COVID-19, angering Beijing.

China has since lifted a series of barriers on Australian exports, though tensions have occasionally flared, including after a Chinese missile test into the Pacific and Beijing's arrest of Chinese-born Australian nationals on spying charges.

In a media briefing after the meeting, Albanese said differences would be discussed "constructively and directly", and a stable relationship was in the interests of both nations.

"It is important that Australia continues to engage in a constructive way with China, manage our differences, but not be defined by them. And we, today, were able to discuss a full range of issues," Albanese said.

Albanese is expected to travel to Beijing later on Friday and will meet Chinese Premier Li Qiang.

He will be accompanied by several top Australian business executives including Rio Tinto's head of iron ore Matt Holcz and BHP's Australia boss Geraldine Slattery for a CEO roundtable with Chinese company executives.

The meeting comes amid increasingly fraught negotiations between Australia's top miners and China's state iron ore buyer, China Mineral Resources Group, as centralisation of its buying increases the country's bargaining power in negotiating contracts.

Australian Resources Minister Madeleine King said this week that any potential manipulation of trade in iron ore would be against international rules and a threat to government revenues.

(Reporting by Liz Lee in Shenzhen and Beijing newsroom and Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by Muralikumar Anantharaman)

data.title: Airwheel Unveils Smart Cabin Luxury Hand 20 inch Carry On Airport Boarding Ai Wheel Suitcase for Every Kind of Traveler Luggage
data.description:
BRUSSELS, BELGIUM, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As air travel, cross-city journeys and business trips become increasingly common, moving through airports, railway stations and large exhibition centers often involves considerable walking and frequent transfers. For travelers carrying luggage, these journeys can be physically demanding. This has created new opportunities for innovation in the traditional luggage industry.

The smart riding cabin suitcase is one response to this evolving travel landscape. By integrating an electric drive system and a rideable structure into conventional luggage, it combines everyday storage with short-distance personal mobility. Rather than simply being pulled from one destination to another, a suitcase can also become an intelligent travel companion that helps users move more conveniently in suitable environments.

With more than 600 global patents, Airwheel has been exploring the intersection of smart mobility and traditional luggage. Through ongoing development in power systems, mechanical engineering and intelligent control, the brand continues to advance the design and functionality of smart riding suitcases.

1. What Is a Smart Riding Luxury Suitcase? Airwheel's Journey Begins with SE3 Scooter Suitcase

What makes a smart riding electric suitcase different from conventional luggage?

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/a558aa53-dba7-45c7-b4b4-270f0cea73f7/1.jpg

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/52bce536-10db-4b25-b781-b1e9483e2cfc/2.jpg

A traditional suitcase relies on wheels and a telescopic handle for manual pulling. A smart riding suitcase retains the essential function of luggage storage while adding an electric drive system and a riding mechanism. When the riding structure is deployed, users can ride the suitcase for short-distance transportation. When riding is not required, the mechanism can be folded away, allowing the suitcase to return to its conventional towing mode.

This combination expands the role of luggage from a passive carrier of personal belongings into a mobility product with additional functionality.

Integrating an electric drive system and a riding mechanism into a compact suitcase is a complex engineering challenge. Designers must balance motor performance, structural stability, storage capacity and ease of operation. The riding components must deploy smoothly and lock securely, while remaining compact enough to be stored when not in use.

Airwheel began exploring this product category with its SE3 smart riding suitcase. The early SE3 brought together an electric drive system, a retractable riding handle, electronic braking and smartphone app control, demonstrating how personal mobility technology could be integrated into a traditional luggage format.

The SE3 marked an important step in Airwheel's development of smart riding luggage. Since then, the company has continued to refine its riding mechanisms, drive systems and user interfaces, gradually building a product portfolio for adults and children, including both 20 inch suitcase and larger checked-luggage models.

2. Advancing the Technology: Making Smart Features Practical for Everyday Travel

The value of a smart suitcase goes beyond adding an electric riding function to traditional luggage. Its development is ultimately about making that function more practical, intuitive and adaptable to real travel situations.

Image: https://ml.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/da7d6574-a644-409f-b9ec-f7f9b3b4f2c4/3.jpg

From Manual Deployment to One-Touch Electric Extension

The riding mechanism is one of the defining features of a smart riding suitcase.

In earlier designs, users needed to manually extend the riding handle and complete the locking process before riding. As the product range evolved, Airwheel introduced automatic locking mechanisms to simplify operation.

The Airwheel SE3SXD Ai Suitcase flagship model takes this development further with an electric dual-extension system.

With a one-touch operation, the motorized front wheel and riding handle can extend and lock into position. After riding, users can activate the retraction function to fold the components back into the suitcase. This allows the product to switch between riding and conventional luggage modes more conveniently.

The progression from manual deployment to automatic locking and then electric dual extension reflects Airwheel's ongoing work to improve mechanical integration and the overall user experience.

Smart App Control and Apple Find My Support

Smart interaction is another important part of Airwheel's product development.

Selected premium models are equipped with a dedicated mobile app, allowing users to access product information and use model-specific functions. Depending on the model, these may include speed adjustment, lighting settings, remote control and cruise control.

Selected models, including the SE3SL+ Boarding Airport Suitcase, SE3SX Cabin Suitcase and SE3SXD Ai Luxury Suitcase, also support Apple's Find My network, providing an additional way to help locate a suitcase.

By combining mechanical innovation with connected features, Airwheel is bringing the interaction capabilities of smart hardware into the traditional luggage category.

Removable 73.26Wh Battery for Greater Travel Flexibility

Battery design is a key consideration for any electric suitcase, particularly when the product is intended for air travel.

Selected Airwheel 20-inch adult smart riding suitcase models use a removable 73.26Wh lithium-ion battery. The modular battery design allows the battery to be detached from the suitcase, giving travelers greater flexibility when managing the product in accordance with airline requirements.

Airwheel's 20-inch models are designed around the dimensions commonly associated with cabin-size luggage, while the 24-inch SE3T Ai Wheel is a larger checked-luggage model. For checked luggage, the battery must be removed and handled according to the applicable airline's procedures.

3. What Should Travelers Know Before Choosing a Smart Riding Suitcase?

Beyond design and technology, practical questions such as riding range, speed, load capacity and suitable environments are important when evaluating a smart riding suitcase.

How Far Can an Airwheel Smart Riding Suitcase Travel on One Charge?

According to Airwheel's product specifications, most adult models offer an estimated riding range of approximately 8 kilometers on a full charge. The larger 24-inch SE3T has an estimated range of approximately 6 kilometers.

These figures are intended for short-distance mobility, such as moving through airport terminals, railway stations, exhibition centers and hotel environments.

Actual range may vary depending on rider weight, surface conditions, ambient temperature, riding speed and usage habits. Low temperatures and heavier loads, for example, may reduce the distance achievable on a single charge.

How Fast Can Different Models Travel?

Airwheel offers different speed configurations across its product range to accommodate different product designs and user requirements.

  • SE3S and SE3T: Maximum speed of up to 13 km/h.
  • SE3miniT: Maximum speed of up to 8 km/h.
  • SE3SL, SE3SL+, SE3SX and SE3SXD: Maximum speed of up to 9.9 km/h.
  • SQ3: Maximum speed of up to 5 km/h.
  • SQ3S: Maximum speed of up to 6.5 km/h.

The children's models use lower speed configurations. Regardless of the model, riders should adjust their speed to pedestrian traffic, surrounding conditions and local venue regulations.

What Is the Maximum Riding Load?

Riding load refers to the maximum rider weight supported by the suitcase when used in riding mode. It is different from the amount of luggage the suitcase can carry internally.

According to Airwheel's specifications, the maximum riding loads vary by model:

  • SE3S, SE3T and SE3miniT: Up to 110 kg.
  • SE3SL, SE3SL+, SE3SX and SE3SXD: Up to 95 kg.
  • SQ3 and SQ3S: Up to 40 kg.

Travelers should check the specifications of their chosen model and follow the corresponding product instructions.

Where Is a Smart Riding Suitcase Best Used?

Airwheel smart riding suitcases are designed primarily for short-distance travel on flat, paved surfaces, where riding is permitted.

Potential use cases include:

  • Moving through large airport terminals.
  • Short-distance transfers in railway stations and transport hubs.
  • Hotel and business travel environments.
  • Large exhibition and convention centers.
  • Other paved areas where electric riding devices are permitted.

When riding is unsuitable or not permitted, users can retract the riding mechanism and move the suitcase in conventional towing mode.

Steep slopes, grass, gravel, stairs and wet or slippery surfaces are not recommended for riding. Airwheel models use an electronic braking system with a buffered braking process rather than an emergency-stop function. Riders should maintain a controlled speed, remain aware of their surroundings and follow the product's safety instructions.

4. A Diverse Product Portfolio for Different Travel Needs

Through continued research and product development, Airwheel has established a product portfolio that includes 20-inch adult cabin-size models, a 24-inch checked-luggage model and smart riding suitcases for children.

20 Inch Adult Smart Cabin Suitcases

The 20-inch range is a central part of Airwheel's smart riding suitcase portfolio. These models are designed for travel scenarios such as airports, railway stations, business trips and exhibition centers.

The Airwheel SE3SXD Ai Luxury Suitcase represents the flagship direction of the range. It features an electric dual-extension system that allows users to deploy or retract the riding components with one-touch operation. It also supports a dedicated mobile app and Apple Find My, with a maximum riding speed of 9.9 km/h.

The SE3SX features an electric retractable front-wheel design, app connectivity and Apple Find My support. Its maximum riding speed is also 9.9 km/h.

The SE3SL and SE3SL+ offer alternative configurations for different user preferences. The SE3miniT adopts a lightweight, non-retractable front-wheel structure designed for flat surfaces, while the SE3S offers a maximum riding speed of up to 13 km/h.

Together, these models provide different combinations of riding performance, mechanical design and smart functionality.

24 Inch Smart Checked Suitcase

For travelers who need more storage capacity, the Airwheel SE3T offers a larger 24-inch format.

The model provides 48 liters of storage capacity and features a 250W motor, a maximum riding speed of 13 km/h and a maximum riding load of 110 kg.

By combining a larger luggage compartment with short-distance electric mobility, the SE3T offers another option for business trips and longer journeys. As a checked-luggage model, its removable battery must be handled in accordance with airline requirements.

Smart Riding Suitcases for Children

Airwheel also extends the smart riding suitcase concept to family travel through its SQ3 and SQ3S children's models.

The SQ3 is designed for children aged 3–6, while the SQ3S is designed for children aged 5–8. Both feature lower-speed configurations and incorporate features such as Bluetooth audio and lighting to create a more engaging travel experience.

With products for adults and children, Airwheel continues to explore a wider range of applications for smart riding luggage.

5. Global Presence: Bringing Smart Mobility Innovation to International Markets

Founded in 2004, Airwheel follows the brand philosophy of "Free Intelligent Life " The company focuses on the research, development and innovation of smart mobility products, bringing electric drive technology, intelligent control and industrial design into everyday transportation and travel products.

Its technology development covers areas including motion control, electric drive systems, intelligent sensing and structural engineering. According to Airwheel's published company information, the brand has accumulated more than 600 global patents, including over 180 patents directly related to smart luggage.

Airwheel products are available in 68 countries and regions, supported by a global retail network of more than 4,600 retail terminals.

The brand has also received recognition in international design and innovation programs, including the US-based IDEA and MUSE awards, IDA, the French Design Awards and the Berlin Design Award, among others. These recognitions reflect Airwheel's continued exploration of product design, structural innovation and smart mobility experiences.

For an international brand, expanding into new markets involves more than increasing product availability. It also requires an understanding of different consumer expectations, airline transportation policies and public-space regulations. Airwheel continues to develop and refine its products with the needs of different markets and travel environments in mind.

6. From Smart Luggage to the Future of Travel

The evolution of luggage—from handheld cases to wheeled suitcases and telescopic-handle designs—has continually changed the way people carry their belongings.

Smart riding suitcases represent another step in this evolution by expanding what traditional luggage can do.

For Airwheel, innovation is not simply about adding more features. It is about applying technology to practical travel challenges and developing products that respond to the way people move through the world.

As travel habits and mobility technologies continue to evolve, Airwheel will keep exploring new possibilities for intelligent hardware in travel and everyday life.

A suitcase can be more than a way to carry belongings. It can become an intelligent companion that connects technology with the journey ahead. This is the direction Airwheel continues to explore.

About Airwheel

Airwheel is a smart mobility brand founded in 2004, dedicated to the research and development of intelligent mobility products. By integrating electric drive technology, intelligent control systems and innovative industrial design, Airwheel develops products that bring new functionality to modern travel and everyday transportation.

Its portfolio includes smart riding suitcases and other intelligent electric mobility products. With a presence in 68 countries and regions, Airwheel continues to advance its work in motion control, electric drive systems, intelligent sensing and product engineering, with the aim of making travel and mobility more convenient through smart technology.

data.title: Exclusive-US should restrict investments in China's aerospace sector, not certify Chinese aircraft, lawmakers say
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The US government should not certify Chinese-made airplanes and pull contracts from defense contractors, including European aerospace manufacturer Airbus, if they do not halt investments in China's aerospace industrial base, a congressional report reviewed by Reuters said.

The House Select Committee on China said in a report Washington should toughen export controls and restrict investments in China's aerospace sector. The report also raised concerns that Western governments did not do enough to contain the rise of China's military air power.

"The US and its allies should strengthen export controls and tighten investment restrictions on the aerospace sector to stop the transfer of vital technology that will empower our foremost adversary," said Representative John Moolenaar, the panel's chair and a Michigan Republican, following a year-long investigation.

Airbus declined to comment.

The report said the FAA should not allow Chinese-manufactured aircraft to fly in the United States, noting that China has never released its report into the 2022 crash of a China Eastern Airlines Boeing aircraft and citing subsidies that China has given to state-owned Chinese aircraft makers, COMAC and AVIC. 

The FAA declined to comment on the report but said it has not certified any Chinese aircraft.

The US Treasury Department should restrict outbound investment into China's aerospace sector and urge allies to follow suit and subject the purchase of US aerospace companies by French firms to heightened scrutiny until they unwind ties to China's "Civil-Military Ecosystem," the report said.

The report said through joint ventures, co-development agreements, and other commercial relationships "American and other Western companies transferred technology, know-how, and industrial capacity" on aerospace that ultimately benefited the Chinese military.

The Chinese embassy in Washington criticized the report. "China has all along opposed moves to overstretch the concept of national security or politicize trade and tech issues," the embassy said.

AEROSPACE COMPANIES NAMED

The report also said Honeywell Aerospace, GE Aerospace, and Collins Aerospace "repeatedly sought and obtained licenses for controlled technology transfers involving PRC (People's Republic of China) military end users and other military-linked entities as part of Chinese commercial aerospace platforms."

Honeywell Aerospace said all of the projects were "fully licensed and approved by the US government. Honeywell Aerospace has and will continue to follow all U.S. export laws and procedures, as is acknowledged in the report."

GE Aerospace said it "takes national security, compliance, and the protection of its intellectual property seriously, and we work closely with the US government."

RTX, which owns Collins Aerospace, said it has "and will continue to follow relevant US laws and regulations, as the report acknowledges."

The report also warned that "unilateral US restrictions would disadvantage American aerospace companies without denying China access to many Western technologies when allied firms backfill the resulting business."

The report said some French companies advertise themselves to Chinese customers as being beyond the reach of US restrictions and said Airbus advertises that it can sell satellite photos without US restrictions.

The report also said French aerospace companies "maintain much stronger ties to the Chinese aerospace industrial base than American companies" and called for a Treasury-led committee to "apply stricter scrutiny to French acquisitions of key American technology until France unwinds its close integration with the Chinese industrial base." 

(Reporting by David Shepardson; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama, Nick Zieminski, Rod Nickel and Kate Mayberry)

data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI rout deepens
data.description:
* Asia stocks on track for worst week since Covid hit

* Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade

* Dollar holds near 19-month peak on safe-haven flows

(Update prices, add analyst comments and context throughout)

By Jiaxing Li and Rae Wee

HONG KONG/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Asian shares fell on Friday, heading for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in the AIsector, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan lost 3.2%, its biggest single-day drop in over a month. The gauge has now sunk 8.3% this week, its worst performance since March 2020.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly drop, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.4% and was set to end the week 7.1% lower. Taiwan shares were down 5% on Friday and 16% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1991.

The moves in Asia followed losses of more than 2% for the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite after Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, saw its shares surge in a historic debut but the euphoria failed to lift other stocks.

"Risk aversion intensified as investors continued to unwind crowded positioning and reassess the broader macro backdrop following Anthropic's record-shattering IPO," said Preston Pagli, markets analyst at Citi.

He added that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) blowout earnings earlier in the week failed to become the reset markets had hoped for, while sentiment deteriorated further after Anthropic's IPO failed to spark a broader rally.

Further adding to the unease, a report on AMD from a media outlet associated with short-selling fund Hunterbrook Capital raised concerns that the chipmaker's ties to Chinese entities, some linked to blacklisted firms, could draw greater US regulatory scrutiny to the sector.

The AI trade has already been battered by Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia ( NVDA ), growing momentum for the anti-data-centre movement following Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections, and concerns over the sector's rising debt loads.

"No one headline drove the roll though some pointed to an AMD short report which tapered overall sentiment. Overall, it just felt like more questions than answers out there today with most wondering what gets this tape to feel better?" said Goldman Sachs analysts in a trading note.

They said asset managers and hedge funds net-sold macro products while they net-bought pockets of consumer and financials, with liquidity remaining poor, which is exacerbating price action.

US stock futures also pointed to further losses, with the S&P 500 futures down 0.2% and Nasdaq futures down 0.6% in Asia on Friday.

DOLLAR EXTENDS RALLY, TREASURY YIELDS DIP ON RISK AVERSION

As risk sentiment took a beating, the US dollar extended its rally on safe-haven bids, while also being supported by growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

The dollar index last traded steady at 103.86, after rising to its highest since April 2025 this week, and is now on track to post its fourth week of gains.

In government debt, US Treasury yields eased as the sharp equity selloff pushed investors toward safe-haven bonds. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes held steady at 5.02%, near a one-week low. The 2-year yield touched 4.749%, compared with a US close of 4.779%.

Oil prices were mostly steady after an earlier spike, as reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus.

Brent crude futures rose 0.4% to $92.37 a barrel but remained on track for a third week of declines.

Non-interest-bearing gold slid 2.5% to $3,533.40 an ounce and was headed for a 9% weekly loss.

(Reporting by Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Edwina Gibbs and Christian Schmollinger)

data.title: Explainer-Could Huang, Nvidia and company's board be held liable over affair scandal?
data.description:
WILMINGTON, Delaware, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Reports that Jensen Huang, the co-founder of AI chip powerhouse Nvidia, had an extramarital affair with a company executive and ties to a suspected Chinese spy have led to his resignation as CEO and sparked investigations by the US securities regulator and FBI, calls for congressional hearings, a review by the company's independent directors and a proposed investor class action lawsuit. 

Below is a look at the potential legal exposure for Huang, Nvidia and the directors of the company, which dominates the global market for computer chips that power the AI economy.

WHAT ARE THE ALLEGATIONS?

Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of ​Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and US intelligence agencies are trying to determine her ties to China's Ministry of State Security, according to two people familiar with the matter. Megaspeed has faced US scrutiny over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips that are subject to US export restrictions.

Huang admitted he was unfaithful to his wife without providing details about the relationship, which led to a drop in Nvidia's stock price. US President Donald Trump said Huang told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy and Huang has not been accused of criminal wrongdoing.

Reuters could not independently verify the intelligence allegation, which China's foreign ministry has said was "groundless." 

Nvidia formed an independent committee of directors that hired the Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to assist in an internal investigation.

Huang resigned on November 11 after reports that he had an extramarital affair with a company executive who reported to him. 

Nvidia sits at the center of the ​technological rivalry between the United States and China. Washington has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China since ​2022. News of the affair has emerged as Democrats seized control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections, propelled in part by anti-AI and anti-corruption sentiment.

WHAT ABOUT FEDERAL SECURITIES FRAUD? 

A proposed class action was filed in San Jose, California, federal court on November 9 alleging the company and Huang defrauded shareholders by concealing Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which Jensen Huang described in an October 30 Bloomberg interview as "normal and not unusual."

Securities fraud plaintiffs must show that Nvidia and Huang knowingly misled investors, that investors relied on those misleading statements and that those misleading statements artificially inflated the stock.

The lawsuit did not specify damages but the stock lost around 20% from its peak to the end of the class period, a decline of around $1 trillion in market value. 

Such lawsuits are often filed in the wake of a company's stock suffering a large drop, and more are likely.

While the vast majority of US public companies have insurance against securities lawsuits, Nvidia does not given its huge financial resources.

WHAT ABOUT STATE LAW VIOLATIONS?

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, a Republican, is investigating whether Huang's actions harmed state pension funds and her office said they were looking at it through a consumer protection lens focused on potential misrepresentations. 

California Attorney General Rob Bonta told Bloomberg that the Nvidia crisis raised red flags and his office could investigate. Bonta's office did not respond to a request for further details.

State officials could use state securities laws to pursue investigations of alleged violations, according to legal experts. New York's Martin Act is considered the most powerful and the state's attorneys general have used it to police Wall Street, including an insider trading case brought this year. The Martin Act also allows the attorney general to pursue criminal claims.

No states have brought claims and the New York attorney general did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

COULD THE SEC STEP IN?

The US Securities and Exchange Commission launched a civil investigation that included whether Nvidia misled investors, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the situation. Reuters has not verified the report. 

The regulator would have a lower burden of proof than a private investor class action and the SEC can obtain alternative remedies, such as barring individuals from serving as officers or directors of public companies.  

In 2022, during the administration of Democratic President Joe Biden, Nvidia settled allegations by the SEC that in 2018 it had made inadequate disclosures regarding the growth of its processors for the gaming market. The company paid a $5.5 million fine but did not admit or deny the allegations. An investor class action lawsuit over the same allegations is ongoing. 

The SEC declined to comment. 

COULD THE BOARD BE HELD LIABLE?

An investor filed a so-called derivative lawsuit on November 11 seeking to hold the board liable for failing to make a good faith effort to oversee the business and Huang. The lawsuit said the board allowed Nvidia to make repeated assurances about the company's dealings with Megaspeed and the board did not act on warning signs about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang until it was public. 

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in the Northern District of California, also said the board lacked independence to investigate Huang.

Huang's resignation could strengthen the board's defenses against derivative lawsuits by showing the directors were acting on signs of misconduct by forcing him out and refusing to consider his return.

Investors, including state pension funds, can also use their shareholder rights to seek internal records to investigate the board and look for potential conflicts.

The board could sue Huang for any fines or securities fraud settlements that result from the scandal. For example, electric truck maker Nikola took legal action and got a judgment of $168 million against its former CEO Trevor Milton.  

CAN SECURITIES FRAUD CARRY CRIMINAL PENALTIES?

Only a small fraction of all securities fraud cases lead to criminal charges, as most violations are handled through civil or administrative enforcement.

But a federal statute, enacted as part of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, criminalizes schemes that knowingly defraud investors through false pretenses. Prosecutors would need to show that Huang intentionally lied to the public about the affair in order to keep Nvidia's stock price from falling, rather than for personal reasons such as avoiding embarrassment.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche also said the FBI was investigating if Alice Huang was a spy. 

If Huang knew about Alice Huang's alleged intelligence connection, he could face criminal liability under the Economic Espionage Act, a 1996 law that punishes the misappropriation of trade secrets to benefit a foreign government.

(Reporting by Tom Hals in Wilmington, Delaware; Additional reporting by Jan Wolfe and Steve Holland; Editing by Nick Zieminski and Noleen Walder)

data.title: Japan's Nikkei falls more than 4% after Anthropic's IPO fails to restore AI confidence
data.description:
(Adds comments, updates stock prices)

By Junko Fujita

TOKYO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Japan's Nikkei stock average fell more than 4% on Friday to touch a seven-month low, as technology shares tumbled after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in AI trade.

The Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to 56,594.94, its lowest level since mid-April, and was down 4.33% to 56,871.78 as of 0210 GMT.

The broader Topix fell 2.89% to 3,711.87.

"There was a high expectation that Anthropic's market debut may lift sentiment for AI-related shares, but that hope faded as its price pared gains," said Hiroyuki Ueno, chief strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management.

Shares of Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, opened 34% higher than the $83 IPO price set on Wednesday. But the stock pared gains and closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price.

In Japan, chip-related Advantest ( ADTTF ) and Tokyo Electron ( TOELF ) slipped 10.15% and 6.07%, respectively. Technology investor SoftBank Group tumbled 14.4% and memory chip maker Kioxia ( KXHCF ) lost 11.62%,

"Investors realise that these chip shares became cheap, but they are afraid to pick them up because they are afraid there may be another dip in the market," said Ueno.

Bucking the trend, insurers rose, with Tokio Marine Holdings ( TKOMF ) rising 3% to become the top percentage gainer on the Nikkei. MS&AD Insurance ( MSADF ) and Sompo Holdings ( NHOLF ) rose 2.83% and 1.71%, respectively.

Drug makers rose, with Takeda Pharmaceutical ( TAK ) and Shionogi & Co ( SGIOF ) gaining 0.63% and 0.4%, respectively.

Of more than 1,500 stocks trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 90% fell, 8% rose and 1% traded flat.

data.title: Lynas shareholder meeting to spotlight CEO hunt next week
data.description:
* Lynas shareholder meeting in Sydney on November 25

* Succession process to replace Amanda Lacaze started in January

* Lynas says highly credentialed candidate withdrew from process

By Melanie Burton

MELBOURNE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The prolonged hunt for a new CEO to lead Lynas Rare Earths ( LYSCF ) will be front and centre at its annual shareholder meeting next week, after the West's top producer of the strategic metals said a favoured candidate withdrew.

Former CEO Amanda Lacaze announced her retirement in January, and some investors say the extended search to replace her has left the company vulnerable to a takeover, especially after a 42% share-price slide from a 15-year high hit in April.

Lynas is the only commercial producer of both light and heavy rare earths outside China and by far the most advanced in building a supply chain from mine to magnet, key to the West's push to diversify procurement for a wide range of industries, from electric vehicles and robotics to defence.

"Considering the barriers to entry and strategic importance of this sector, corporate appeal is likely to be the highest it's been in some time," said Sam Berridge, a portfolio manager with Perennial Partners in Perth.

Lynas chairman John Humphrey said last month he expected to announce a new CEO before the annual general meeting in Sydney on November 25. The board suspended the search earlier this year while it was in talks on a merger that did not go ahead. The hunt was delayed further after a contender pulled out.

"Lynas Chairman, John Humphrey, has previously confirmed that a highly credentialed candidate withdrew from the process for personal reasons prior to being interviewed by the full Board," said head of investor relations Daniel Havas.

Fund managers said that suggested the search may extend past next week.

"Lynas is a unique company, and the Board wants to ensure the right appointment is made," Havas said by email. "The Board has great confidence in our Interim CEO and the highly experienced senior leadership team to continue to run operations and implement the Towards 2030 growth strategy."

Pol Le Roux, previously chief operating officer, has acted as interim CEO since the end of June.

TOUGH GIG

Finding a replacement for "a superstar CEO" such as Amanda Lacaze, who was at the helm for 12 years, may prove tough, said Matthew Hope, a resources analyst with Ord Minnett.

The company's 2030 growth plan and October deal to buy a rare earths mine in Brazil will make it hard for a new CEO to make their mark, while development plans will be costly, suggesting it may be hard to boost Lynas' share price and earn incentives, he said.

Investors have been unimpressed by how long the search has taken, with some suggesting it has left the company vulnerable to a predator. Major gold producer Newmont ( NEM ) seized a chance to buy Australia's biggest gold producer Newcrest Mining when it was without a permanent CEO in 2023.

While Lynas shares have held up better than other critical minerals companies hit by concerns about a slowdown in data centre growth, they are trading on a forward EV/EBITDA multiple broadly in line with 10-year lows, Perennial's Berridge said.

Meanwhile, demand for rare earth metals remains solid, backed by a US push to replace missile inventories, robust demand growth for industrial robots and steady global EV sales, he said.

(Reporting by Melanie Burton; Editing by Sonali Paul)

data.title: Oil prices edge higher as Houthi attacks on Riyadh raise supply concerns
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Oil prices edged higher on Friday, though set for a weekly decline, as concerns over supply disruptions grew following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.    

Brent crude futures rose 24 cents, or 0.3%, to $92.22 a barrel by 0118 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures for December climbed 19 cents, or 0.2%, to $83.40 a barrel, while the more-active January contract gained 20 cents, or 0.2%, to $82.64. 

Both benchmarks settled little changed on Thursday but Brent is set for a 3.5% decline for the week while the December WTI contract is set for a 6% weekly drop as expectations of a supply surplus grew because crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels. Brent and WTI are set to fall for the third week in a row. 

"Concerns over Middle Eastern crude oil supplies have resurfaced due to attacks on Riyadh by the Houthis, prompting buying," said Satoru Yoshida, a commodity analyst with Rakuten Securities.

"Expectations that coordinated production cuts will continue at the OPEC+ meeting later this month are also providing support," he said.

The Iran-aligned Houthi movement fired missiles at Riyadh, the latest blow to the kingdom in its war with the Houthis.

Two oil tankers also hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and "exploded" and "are burning", Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said in a statement carried by state media on Thursday.

OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their 2027 output policy. The group comprises the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies such as Russia.

The Middle East conflict has caused the biggest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade and could cut world oil demand by more than 4% by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday.

In Russia, crude oil output could fall again as Ukrainian attacks on refineries and export infrastructure intensify, analysts and traders say. Ukrainian drone attacks have slashed Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, Reuters reported on Wednesday.

Separately on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin said that Moscow would hit back hard after Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and Crimea for a third time this week and said he was dropping any idea of a moratorium on attacking energy sectors and shipping.

(Reporting by Yuka Obayashi; Editing by Christian Schmollinger)

data.title: Samsung Electronics appoints new head for its memory chip business
data.description:
* Former memory development head to lead memory business

* Samsung replaces System LSI head, chip CTO

* Shares slump as Anthropic IPO fails to lift AI sentiment

(Add quotes from Samsung statement, further appointments, shares, analyst comment)

SEOUL, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ) on Friday said it has appointed a new chief for its memory chip business as part of a management reshuffle, coming as surging demand for AI chips powers the South Korean technology major to record profit.

The chipmaker promoted Hwang Sang-joon to president and head of memory, having previously led memory development, including for chips such as dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

Hwang will "help strengthen the competitiveness of memory products in the AI era," Samsung said in a statement.

It also said it "promoted vice presidents who spearheaded record-breaking semiconductor performance and enhanced technological competitiveness" as part of "generational leadership change".

Samsung posted a 15-fold jump in quarterly chip profit for the third quarter, as a rush to build data centres for artificial intelligence-powered applications and services strained the supply of AI chips and pumped up prices.

Co-CEO and Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun will continue to oversee the broader device solutions division, which includes memory and logic chips, and "focus on enhancing future businesses such as foundry," Samsung said.

The chipmaker also promoted US chip head Cho Sang-yeun, appointing him as head of its System LSI Business, which designs logic chips for tech firms.

"With his strong global customer relationship, he is expected to expand the customer base for the System LSI Business," Samsung said.

Samsung also promoted its head of chip process development for memory and foundry, Lee Jong-myeong, as chief technology officer of its device solutions division.

With the latest reshuffle, Samsung is likely to boost its chip contract manufacturing business and diversify its customer base beyond Nvidia ( NVDA ) to Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Alphabet's Google, as hyperscalers are likely to reduce reliance on AI leader Nvidia ( NVDA ) following the resignation of scandal-hit Jensen Huang as CEO, said Park Ju-gun, head of corporate analysis firm Leaders Index.

NEW MOBILE HEAD

Shares of Samsung have fluctuated with broader on-off sentiment toward AI, which commentators bill as world-changing but at huge cost in terms of infrastructure. They slumped more than 5% on Friday in wider tech selloff after Anthropic's super-sized IPO failed to revitalise AI enthusiasm.

Samsung also appointed President Choi Won-joon as head of its mobile device business. Choi was formerly chief operating officer and led the launch of the Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold8 series smartphones.

Challenges in mobile devices include rising memory chip prices and competition particularly from Chinese rivals.

data.title: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI trade gloom fails to abate
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Asian shares slid on Friday to be on track for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in AI trades, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares lost 2.5%, poised for a six-day losing streak. The gauge has now declined 7% this week, its worst performance since March 2020.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly drop, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.7% and was set to end the week 7.5% lower.

The moves in Asia followed losses of more than 2% for the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite.

Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, saw its shares surge more than 30% in a historic debut but the euphoria failed to lift other boats.

"Anthropic's blockbuster IPO proved not enough to assuage the overall concern about the outlook for the AI trade and equities more broadly," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

The wider AI sector has been bruised by the exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia ( NVDA ) as well as additional momentum for the anti-data-center movement in the wake of the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.

Unease about mounting debt loads in the sector and warnings that AI threatens human extinction have also hit sentiment.

Rodda said that with the AI trade fading and Fed rate hikes seen likely, general market sentiment is shaky and the risk is that this bearishness begins to drag stocks even lower.

US stock futures also point to further losses, with the S&P 500 futures down 0.4% and Nasdaq futures down 0.7% in Asia on Friday.

DOLLAR EXTENDS RALLY, TREASURY YIELDS DIP ON RISK AVERSION

As risk sentiment took a beating, the US dollar extended its rally, also supported by growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

The dollar index last traded steady at 103.86, after hitting its strongest level since April 2025 this week.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

In government debt, US Treasury yields eased as the sharp equity selloff pushed investors toward safe-haven bonds. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes held steady at 5.026%, near a one-week low. The two-year yield touched 4.749%, compared with a US close of 4.779%.

Oil prices were mostly steady after an earlier spike, as reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus.

Brent crude futures settled flat at $91.98 a barrel, on track for a third straight week of decline.

Non-interest-bearing gold dipped 0.6% to $3,601.40 an ounce and was headed for a 7.3% weekly loss.

(Reporting by Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong; Editing by Edwina Gibbs)

data.title: Dollar near 19-month peak as AI jitters sap risk appetite
data.description:
SHANGHAI/SINGAPORE, Nov 20 (Reuters) - The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, having risen over the past eight sessions as jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets, while the yen steadied after Japanese inflation data.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, its strongest since early April 2025, and was on track for a fourth straight week of gains. The rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy. Markets are now pricing in a 25-basis-point hike in December and a small chance of a larger move.

The AI trade continued to set the mood, with Anthropic's historic market debut doing little to revive sentiment as US equities fell sharply overnight.

Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a volatile stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

"Risk aversion intensified, supporting the safe-haven dollar and driving demand for US Treasuries," OCBC analysts said in a note. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks."

The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to a one-week low of 5.016% in early Asia trade and is down 10 basis points on the week.

Adding to the dollar's strength were hawkish signals from the Fed. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own, and that the booming rollout of AI technology could further boost inflation the Fed would have to counteract.

The yen edged up 0.1% against the dollar to 159.50. Data showed Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that cement the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3094, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0972. The Aussie hovered close to a one-year low of $0.66476.

China's offshore yuan slipped 0.4% overnight, breaking from its recent pattern of calm moves, with no obvious catalyst. China left key benchmark lending rates unchanged in November for an 18th consecutive month.

(Reporting by Li Gu in Shanghai and Rae Wee in Singapore; Editing by Tom Hogue)

data.title: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - Taiwan's TSMC is tightening restrictions on Chinese chip designers, suspending some previously permitted advanced manufacturing orders and generally limiting affected customers to older chipmaking technology, according to two people familiar with the matter.

The move could close one of the last remaining routes for Chinese companies to produce powerful AI processors, complicating Beijing's efforts to develop domestic alternatives to chips designed by Nvidia ( NVDA ) and manufactured by TSMC.

The world's largest contract chipmaker has instructed that affected orders using manufacturing processes of 16 nanometres and below be halted unless customers obtain US export licences, the people said.

Chinese designers will generally be limited to older 28-nanometre and 40-nanometre processes, provided their chips do not use high-bandwidth memory (HBM) or require advanced packaging, according to TSMC guidance reviewed by the two people.

Most leading AI chips are produced using 7-nanometre processes or smaller, enabling faster and more energy-efficient performance. HBM allows processors to handle the vast data volumes required by AI applications, while advanced packaging integrates chips and memory to boost computing power.

US CLOSES MANUFACTURING ROUTE

The restrictions follow new US Commerce Department rules that took effect on Thursday, removing a compliance route that had allowed some Chinese designers to access advanced manufacturing services without individual export licences.

Previously, TSMC could check the computing power and other technical characteristics of certain Chinese chip designs to determine whether they fell outside US export controls.

Under the new rules, TSMC can no longer use that verification process for affected Chinese customers. Their advanced chips are instead presumed to be covered by US controls, requiring export licences unless an exception applies.

The Financial Times first reported on Thursday that TSMC and South Korea's Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ) had suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers following the new restrictions.

CHINA'S AI CHIP AMBITIONS

The measures could particularly affect Chinese companies developing alternatives to Nvidia's ( NVDA ) processors, including independent chip designers and technology giants that have developed in-house chips.

A US government list of approved chip designers includes Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD, Apple and Taiwanese companies MediaTek and Realtek, but no mainland Chinese firms.

Some Chinese AI chip designers still had access to TSMC's 7-nanometre manufacturing technology before Thursday, a separate source with direct knowledge of the matter said. Reuters could not independently verify the arrangements under which those chips were manufactured.

TSMC's guidance also requires closer scrutiny of customers' operating locations, parent companies, major shareholders, packaging providers and shipping routes, the people said.

The checks extend to orders placed through overseas subsidiaries or intermediaries, including entities in Taiwan, the US, Europe, Japan and Southeast Asia.

(Reporting by Pan Che and Wen-Yee Lee. Editing by Eduardo Baptista and Mark Potter)
